first_line_carrier_force.Soryu_note: Available in this rerun; the old three-carrier holding-force line is superseded for this working branch.
movement: 22-24 Jan: Pacific-priority alert and departure/closure from Truk-area readiness rather than routine training dispersal.
25-29 Jan: radio-disciplined holding position west of the Marshalls, retaining westward egress and staying outside routine US island-strike search expectation.
30-31 Jan: after firm carrier contact, limited eastward closure is authorized but no strike without a fresh enough target and acceptable other-TG uncertainty.

secondary_carriers.posture: Truk/Ponape rear-deck reserve and ferry/CAP/recovery depth. Not added to the first-line strike by default.
secondary_carriers.use_if_battle_opens: CAP/search relief, cross-deck recovery, reinforcement ferry, and a bounded follow-on package if geometry remains favorable.

submarine_network.delta_from_old_line: I-175 is not locked into the superseded GALVANIC Pierce-hit/heavy-repair path, adding one plausible effective patrol asset. No wolfpack datalink is created.
submarine_network.reporting_rule: Time/position/type/course/speed/confidence reports are fused with DF, water-air and traffic analysis; a boat may report instead of taking a poor shot.

Yamamoto_decision_rule: The four-deck force makes intervention more credible, but the fleet is not committed merely because one US TG is seen. GO requires fresh target geometry, evidence of US mission split/recovery state, acceptable uncertainty about other TGs, and a safe Japanese recovery/egress window.
